summary.headline: Pace Digitek Q2 FY27 revenue rose 51.5% YoY to Rs 808 crore and FY27 revenue guidance was raised to Rs 3,300-3,500 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue was Rs 808 crore (+51.5% YoY, +45.5% QoQ) and H1 revenue was Rs 1,364 crore (+51.4%), with energy about 80% and telecom about 20%. Q2 EBITDA rose 68.5% YoY to Rs 159 crore and PAT rose 43.3% to Rs 97 crore, though management said margins were flattered by a higher telecom services mix. Borrowings rose to Rs 1,371 crore from Rs 961 crore in March 2026, driven by build-to-operate (BOT) assets, and net debt-to-equity moved to 0.35x. Management raised FY27 revenue guidance but kept FY28 at Rs 4,000-4,200 crore, and said it has paused new BOT projects without external investment.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 28 crore in Q1 FY27

financial_highlights.value: Rs 10,735 crore (energy Rs 8,528 crore; telecom Rs 2,208 crore)
financial_highlights.change: H1 inflows Rs 2,437 crore (energy Rs 2,173 crore; telecom Rs 265 crore)

segments.name: Energy (BESS)
segments.commentary: Energy contributed about 80% of H1 revenue; energy EBITDA margin is 12-13% per management, and the combined EBITDA margin was flattered by telecom services. H1 BESS commissioning was about 875 MWh, with 1.8 GWh delivered to customers to date.

segments.name: Telecom
segments.commentary: Telecom contributed about 20% of revenue, with EBITDA margin around 20% (20-23% on projects, about 25% on O&M). More than 8,000 BSNL sites were commissioned and entered a 5-year O&M phase.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance raised to Rs 3,300-3,500 crore from Rs 3,200-3,400 crore.
FY28 revenue guidance unchanged at Rs 4,000-4,200 crore; management said it sees 'a much better guidance' than provided but has not revised it.
FY28 PAT margin guided at about 10% (management later said 10-11%), down from the 11-12% level seen in H1 FY27, which was helped by telecom turnkey projects.
Blended EBITDA margin expected at 16-17% as energy mix rises; container in-house fabrication expected to cut BESS cost by 4-5% gross and add about 1.5-2% at EBITDA level.
Build-to-operate revenue expected at Rs 325-375 crore in FY28, after Rs 197 crore from the current project and about Rs 200 crore from two projects commissioning by March 2027.
Peak debt expected at around Rs 1,100 crore of additional borrowing by March 2027, with about Rs 1,600 crore of back-to-back BOT assets.
C&I to target about 30% of energy revenue in the next financial year (FY28); C&I margins expected to lift blended EBITDA by at least 1-2%.
capex_capacity: BESS manufacturing capacity expanded from 2.5 GWh to 5 GWh in August 2026; production currently running at full 5 GWh. About 844 MWh produced in H1 FY27, equal to 94% of FY26 output.
Expansion to 10 GWh: an additional 5 GWh setup to be completed in Q3 FY27, with production starting in Q4 and about one quarter needed to reach full utilisation.
In-house BESS container facility: trial production from November 2026 and full-scale production from January 2027, expected to meet about 50% of container requirements.
BESS volume target of about 200 containers per quarter; Q2 sold about 91 containers plus 10 in stock (about 100), and Q3 target is slightly below 200.

Build-to-operate asset stood at Rs 1,311 crore at 30 Sep 2026; about 60% commissioned, with completion expected December 2026 or January 2027. Management has paused new BOT projects absent external investment.
4 GWh cell manufacturing (PLI) tendering expected to complete by mid-November 2026; cell plant to start in the next financial year, with technology transfer still under study at the R&D centre.
demand_pricing: Management sees BESS demand of about 30-35 GWh in FY27, rising to about 236 GWh by FY32.
Bidding competition has eased: about 6-8 participants per tender now versus 25-30 earlier; management said margin pressure persists but is smaller.
Lithium-ion cell prices rose about 20% in the prior quarter, hurting energy project margins; prices are now falling and expected to stabilise. Tenders bid over the last 3-4 months use the new prices.
Landed Chinese BESS price is roughly in line with Pace's manufacturing cost plus margin.
From January 2027, about 6% export rebate cut on Chinese cell imports; management expects lower cell prices to offset it.
Standalone EBITDA margin fell due to early-stage MAHAGENCO solar supply-and-erection and Bondada balance-of-systems projects with higher initial mobilisation costs.
Receivable days were about 286 at March 2026; management expects receivable cycle near 150 days and payables of 60-90 days, for a net working capital cycle of 90-120 days.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp EBITDA margin improvement and how should margins trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it targets 17-19% EBITDA margin and that H1 was lifted by a larger telecom services share; energy margins are 12-13% and telecom about 20%. Blended margin is expected to fall to 16-17% as energy grows.

qa_highlights.question: Q2 container volumes and Q3-Q4 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About 100 containers in Q2 (91 sold, 10 stocked) on an unchanged 2.5 GWh base, because the expanded capacity only started commercial production in September. Q3 is targeted at slightly below 200 containers.

qa_highlights.question: Benefit from in-house container fabrication?
qa_highlights.answer: Container cost expected to fall about 25%, BESS overall cost 4-5% at gross level, and about 1.5-2% at EBITDA level.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Q2 standalone and energy margins decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Two new solar projects (MAHAGENCO and Bondada) carry high initial mobilisation costs, plus a 20% rise in lithium-ion cell prices last quarter and early-stage costs at the new BESS capacity. Management expects a slight recovery in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10 GWh capacity supported by enough BESS demand, and how is FY28 guidance framed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand of 30-35 GWh in FY27 and 236 GWh by FY32 supports capacity; the 10 GWh is to reach full utilisation one quarter after Q4 start. FY28 guidance was not revised but management expects better. Revenue realisation is spread over about 2 years because most product goes into EPC and BOT projects.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working-capital outlook for receivables and payables?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables are falling as telecom retentions are collected, and management expects receivable days near 150 and payables of 60-90 days. Consolidated payables fell from about Rs 1,800 crore to Rs 1,500 crore, with a target of Rs 800-900 crore.

risks_watch: Working-capital intensity: H1 operating cash flow was negative about Rs 542 crore including finance lease receivables; management says it is positive excluding them.
Debt build: borrowings rose by Rs 410 crore in H1, with about Rs 1,100 crore more planned by March 2027, so finance costs and net debt-to-equity may keep rising.
Margin dilution: management guides FY28 PAT margin to about 10% as the energy mix grows, while energy EBITDA is 12-13%.
Execution timelines: 10 GWh expansion, in-house container plant (January 2027 full-scale), BOT completion (December 2026-January 2027), and cell manufacturing plans all depend on schedule.
Lithium-ion cell price volatility and the January 2027 export rebate cut on Chinese cells; the technology-transfer timeline for cells is still unclear.
C&I ramp: 30% of energy revenue targeted in FY28, but bigger C&I orders are only expected by end-Q3 or Q4 FY27.
Receivable and payable days remain high (debtor days about 286 at March 2026), and the reconciliation given on the call was not fully clear to the analyst.
key_quotes: And we are very confident about the guidance we have provided.
Next year's guidance, we have not revised it as on today, but we are definitely seeing a much better guidance than what we have provided.
We have paused the build-to-operate project unless otherwise we get some external investment.
I would request you to see the consolidated payable.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, the 10 GWh expansion and FY27 guidance raise, and the closing remarks. Cautious and sometimes evasive on the working-capital and payables reconciliation, FY28 guidance (not revised), and margin trajectory, which shifted between answers (PAT about 10% vs 10-11%).

adds.what: BESS manufacturing expansion from 2.5 GWh to 5 GWh (already done, Aug 2026)
Additional 5 GWh BESS line to take capacity to 10 GWh
In-house BESS container facility, about 50% of container needs (trial from Nov 2026, full scale Jan 2027)
Build-to-operate assets: about 60% of Rs 1,311 crore commissioned, rest by Dec 2026/Jan 2027
4 GWh cell manufacturing (PLI) plant, tendering to finish mid-Nov 2026, start next FY

growth.why: FY27 revenue guidance raised to Rs 3,300-3,500 crore (midpoint ~Rs 3,400 crore, ~41% growth implied vs FY26 base) backed by full 5 GWh utilisation, a 10 GWh line due Q4, and an executable order book of Rs 10,735 crore; FY28 Rs 4,000-4,200 crore held, PAT margin guided down to ~10%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides blended EBITDA margin down to 16-17% from H1's flattering telecom-led level (Q2 EBITDA Rs 159 crore on Rs 808 crore revenue, roughly 20%), and FY28 PAT margin about 10% vs 11-12% in H1 FY27, as energy (12-13% EBITDA) grows; C&I mix adds only 1-2% at EBITDA level, offset partly by in-house containers cutting BESS cost 4-5% gross.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: BESS capacity doubled from 2.5 to 5 GWh in Aug 2026 and running at full 5 GWh, with the additional 5 GWh line (to 10 GWh) under construction for completion in Q3 FY27 and production from Q4; 844 MWh produced in H1 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 BESS output was about 100 containers vs target of 200 per quarter, with Q3 targeted slightly below 200 and 10 GWh capacity starting Q4; executable order book Rs 10,735 crore (energy Rs 8,528 crore) and FY27 demand seen at 30-35 GWh support volumes.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is at 100% of the 5 GWh base, and the 10 GWh expansion is under way, but management has paused new BOT projects absent external investment, so the next announcement is more likely to be cell/PLI-linked (4 GWh, start next FY) than BOT.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance was already raised to Rs 3,300-3,500 crore (H1 revenue Rs 1,364 crore, +51.4%), and management said it sees 'a much better guidance' for FY28 but has not revised the Rs 4,000-4,200 crore range.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Execution risk on the 10 GWh line, in-house container plant (full scale Jan 2027), BOT completion (Dec 2026-Jan 2027) and receivables (Rs 2,177 crore, ~286 debtor days at March 2026) could slip, while net debt-to-equity rose to 0.35x from 0.09x.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: 4 GWh cell manufacturing (PLI) tender to close mid-Nov 2026 with cell plant to start in the next financial year, plus in-house container facility full-scale from January 2027 (about 50% of container needs).

rows.label: Receivables and payables normalisation
rows.why: Management targets receivable days near 150 and payables of 60-90 days (net cycle 90-120 days) from about 286 receivable days at March 2026, with consolidated receivables down to Rs 2,177 crore from Rs 2,442 crore; H1 operating cash flow was negative about Rs 542 crore incl. finance lease receivables, and the reconciliation was unclear.

rows.label: Debt build for BOT assets
rows.why: Borrowings rose to Rs 1,371 crore from Rs 961 crore in H1, with about Rs 1,100 crore more planned by March 2027 against Rs 1,600 crore of back-to-back BOT assets, so finance costs (Rs 36 crore in Q2 vs Rs 28 crore in Q1) rise further.

rows.label: Bidding competition and cell price relief
rows.why: Bidders per tender fell to 6-8 from 25-30, and lithium cell prices (up ~20% last quarter) are now falling, though the January 2027 6% export rebate cut on Chinese cells is a partial offset.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the 10 GWh expansion and the FY27 guidance raise, but cautious or evasive on working capital and payables reconciliation, FY28 guidance (not revised), and margin trajectory (PAT about 10% vs 10-11%); analysts pushed on these points.
